R01.text: Sleep timing, duration (~470 min), steps (~8000), resting HR (~56 bpm) and RMSSD (~45 ms) stayed stable versus your 28-day baseline. However, recorded active minutes dropped sharply from ~54 to ~9 per day, with low-movement minutes rising from ~450 to ~602. This pattern may reflect a change in how movement was captured rather than a true activity decline.

R03.text: Over 28 baseline days, sleep averaged 470 min (start ~22:50, end 07:00), steps ~8015, activity ~54 min/day, low movement ~450 min, RHR 56 bpm, RMSSD 45 ms. In the 14-day window, activity dropped sharply to ~9 min/day (-83%) and low movement rose to ~602 min (+34%), while sleep, steps (~8029), RHR, and RMSSD remained stable. Evening activity intervals shortened from ~50-60 min to ~8-12 min; daytime low-movement blocks lengthened from ~45 min to ~60 min. No weekday/weekend differences emerged. Paired correlations were weak throughout.

R04.text: During the 28-day baseline, sleep averaged 470 min (~22:50-07:00), steps ~8015, activity ~54 min, low movement ~450 min, RHR 56 bpm, and RMSSD 45 ms. In the 14-day window, sleep timing, duration (+1 min), steps (+14), RHR (+0.2 bpm), and RMSSD (-0.1 ms) remained stable. Activity duration dropped sharply by 45 min/day to a persistent mean of 9 min, with evening activity intervals shortening from ~55 min to ~9 min. Low movement increased correspondingly by 152 min/day to ~602 min. These changes began immediately on day 1 of the window and persisted throughout without recovery. No weekday/weekend differences emerged. Baseline RHR-RMSSD correlation was weak; window correlations remained negligible.

R06.text: Your sleep stayed stable across the 14-day window, averaging about 471 minutes and ending consistently at 07:00, matching your 28-day baseline. Steps held near 8,030/day. However, recorded active minutes dropped sharply from a baseline average of 54 to about 9 per day, with evening activity blocks shortening from roughly 50–60 minutes to 8–12 minutes. Correspondingly, low-movement minutes rose by about 152 per day. Resting heart rate (around 56 bpm) and HRV RMSSD (around 45 ms) remained stable. The large shift in daytime movement structure did not coincide with changes in sleep or heart metrics. Because active-minute intensity is unknown, this may reflect a change in how movement was recorded rather than overall exertion.

audit.audit_limitations: This audit is a provisional LLM analysis of synthetic wearable data against anonymous text representations. No representation text, knowledge snippet, or derived statistic constitutes clinical evidence, diagnosis, or ground truth. The PROVISIONAL_LLM_GOLD relevance labels are fallible. Intensity labels are 'unknown' for all activity intervals, preventing any assessment of exertion level. Low movement is not confirmed sitting posture per K068. Arithmetic probe seeds are generic calculations applied uniformly and do not validate causal claims. The audit cannot determine whether observed metric changes reflect behavioral shifts, device artifacts, or other unmeasured factors.
